issue.title: fix: replace blocking Condvar pool with async Semaphore
issue.body:
The SQLite connection pool used std::sync::Condvar to wait for free connections, which blocks the OS thread. Under the default pool size of 1, concurrent requests can block all Tokio worker threads, deadlocking the runtime the task holding the connection can never be scheduled to release it. Replace with tokio::sync::Semaphore so waiters yield to the async runtime instead of blocking.

comment.body:
I know my ai flagged: 

## Summary
I reviewed PR #1808 in `cashubtc/cdk`. The PR refactors database connection pooling logic inside `cdk-sql-common/src/pool.rs` by switching from threading primitives (`Condvar`) to asynchronous Rust semantics using `tokio::sync::Semaphore`. In doing so, it introduces a vulnerability: the `get_timeout` function, which is supposed to wait asynchronously up to a configured `timeout` duration for an available connection, completely ignores the `timeout` parameter during semaphore acquisition (`self.semaphore.clone().acquire_owned().await`). Under load or exhaustion, this causes the task to block indefinitely rather than returning the expected `Error::Timeout`. This breaks the system's ability to gracefully degrade or fail fast when limits are hit, leading to resource exhaustion, starvation of other dependent tasks, and potential deadlocks in production environments, making this a high-severity DoS vulnerability introduced by this PR.

I think there were some other things last time I asked my agent to review it as well.

What should be the behavior @thesimplekid when the wallet has recent key info, but the user requests an online send and the fetching of the key fails? [Right now](https://github.com/cashubtc/cdk/blob/e35d15d3db0195dbb1b40020d0778493105db9eb/crates/cdk/src/wallet/send/saga/mod.rs#L135-L139) we wait for the `refresh_keysets` to finish, completely pausing until the requests fails. Maybe it can do a best effort and load the keys in parallel if the cache is not empty, and wait otherwise.

Regarding your issue, @TheMhv, I think that what is missing is loading the Mint info and creating the data the first time. Great catch.

[We are persisting all the information](https://github.com/cashubtc/cdk/blob/e35d15d3db0195dbb1b40020d0778493105db9eb/crates/cdk/src/wallet/mint_metadata_cache.rs#L266), but we are reading not reading from the database. A proper fix would load from the database [here](https://github.com/cashubtc/cdk/blob/e35d15d3db0195dbb1b40020d0778493105db9eb/crates/cdk/src/wallet/mint_metadata_cache.rs#L326) and only run this [bit](https://github.com/cashubtc/cdk/blob/e35d15d3db0195dbb1b40020d0778493105db9eb/crates/cdk/src/wallet/mint_metadata_cache.rs#L328)  if the cache is empty or stale.

issue.title: Migrate INTEGER/BIGINT columns storing u64 values to TEXT
issue.body:
### Description

Cashu amounts are u64, but neither SQLite nor PostgreSQL has an unsigned 64-bit integer type. Both INTEGER and BIGINT are signed, so values above `i64::MAX` silently overflow when cast to i64. This PR stores all amount-like columns as TEXT instead, eliminating the risk of truncation entirely.

Once columns become TEXT, PostgreSQL refuses to do arithmetic on them; expressions like total_issued + EXCLUDED.total_issued simply fail. Even with SQLite, casting large text values back to integers for math is unreliable. Rather than patching the SQL with ever more complex `CAST/COALESCE` chains, this PR moves all arithmetic into Rust. Each keyset amounts update now reads the current value, adds the delta with checked_add (which returns an explicit error on overflow instead of wrapping silently), and writes the result back. The same applies to SUM() aggregations — amounts are fetched as individual rows and summed in Rust.

A secondary fix handles PostgreSQL's `::` cast syntax (`column::TYPE`), which the SQL parser was misinterpreting as a named bind parameter.

As a next step, amounts should be streamed from storage rather than loaded as full result sets into memory, and all math should be performed in the mint or wallet, outside the storage layer.

+/// Current totals for a single keyset, as stored in the `keyset_amounts` table.
+struct KeysetAmounts {
+    total_issued: u64,
+    total_redeemed: u64,
+    fee_collected: u64,
+}
+
+/// Fetches the current `keyset_amounts` row for the given keyset, returning
+/// `None` if no row exists yet.
+async fn get_keyset_amounts<C>(conn: &C, keyset_id: &Id) -> Result<Option<KeysetAmounts>, Error>
+where
+    C: DatabaseExecutor + Send + Sync,
+{
+    let row = query(
+        r#"SELECT total_issued, total_redeemed, fee_collected FROM keyset_amounts WHERE keyset_id = :keyset_id"#,
+    )?
+    .bind("keyset_id", keyset_id.to_string())
+    .fetch_one(conn)
+    .await?;
+
+    match row {
+        Some(row) => {
+            unpack_into!(let (total_issued, total_redeemed, fee_collected) = row);
+            Ok(Some(KeysetAmounts {
+                total_issued: column_as_number!(total_issued),
+                total_redeemed: column_as_number!(total_redeemed),
+                fee_collected: column_as_number!(fee_collected),
+            }))
+        }
+        None => Ok(None),
+    }
+}
+
+/// Builds an INSERT ... ON CONFLICT upsert query that only overwrites the
+/// specified column, leaving the others at their INSERT defaults.
+fn upsert_query(column: &str) -> String {
+    format!(
+        r#"
+        INSERT INTO keyset_amounts (keyset_id, total_issued, total_redeemed, fee_collected)
+        VALUES (:keyset_id, :total_issued, :total_redeemed, :fee_collected)
+        ON CONFLICT (keyset_id)
+        DO UPDATE SET {column} = :{column}
+        "#
+    )
+}
+
+/// Writes the given amounts back to `keyset_amounts`, inserting or updating
+/// the target column.
+async fn upsert_keyset_amounts<C>(
+    conn: &C,
+    keyset_id: &Id,
+    amounts: &KeysetAmounts,
+    column: &str,
+) -> Result<(), Error>
+where
+    C: DatabaseExecutor + Send + Sync,
+{
+    query(&upsert_query(column))?
+        .bind("keyset_id", keyset_id.to_string())
+        .bind("total_issued", amounts.total_issued)
+        .bind("total_redeemed", amounts.total_redeemed)
+        .bind("fee_collected", amounts.fee_collected)
+        .execute(conn)
+        .await?;
+    Ok(())
+}
+
+/// Adds `delta` to `total_issued` for the given keyset.
+///
+/// Reads the current value from the database, performs the addition in Rust
+/// with overflow checking, and writes the result back.
+pub(crate) async fn increment_total_issued<C>(
+    conn: &C,
+    keyset_id: &Id,
+    delta: u64,
+) -> Result<(), Error>
+where
+    C: DatabaseExecutor + Send + Sync,
+{
+    let mut amounts = get_keyset_amounts(conn, keyset_id)
+        .await?
+        .unwrap_or(KeysetAmounts {
+            total_issued: 0,
+            total_redeemed: 0,
+            fee_collected: 0,
+        });

+/// specified column, leaving the others at their INSERT defaults.
+fn upsert_query(column: &str) -> String {
+    format!(
+        r#"
+        INSERT INTO keyset_amounts (keyset_id, total_issued, total_redeemed, fee_collected)
+        VALUES (:keyset_id, :total_issued, :total_redeemed, :fee_collected)
+        ON CONFLICT (keyset_id)
+        DO UPDATE SET {column} = :{column}
+        "#
+    )
+}
+
+/// Writes the given amounts back to `keyset_amounts`, inserting or updating
+/// the target column.
+async fn upsert_keyset_amounts<C>(
+    conn: &C,
+    keyset_id: &Id,
+    amounts: &KeysetAmounts,
+    column: &str,
+) -> Result<(), Error>
+where
+    C: DatabaseExecutor + Send + Sync,
+{
+    query(&upsert_query(column))?
+        .bind("keyset_id", keyset_id.to_string())
+        .bind("total_issued", amounts.total_issued)
+        .bind("total_redeemed", amounts.total_redeemed)
+        .bind("fee_collected", amounts.fee_collected)
+        .execute(conn)
+        .await?;
+    Ok(())
+}
+
+/// Adds `delta` to `total_issued` for the given keyset.
+///
+/// Reads the current value from the database, performs the addition in Rust
+/// with overflow checking, and writes the result back.
+pub(crate) async fn increment_total_issued<C>(
+    conn: &C,
+    keyset_id: &Id,
+    delta: u64,
+) -> Result<(), Error>
+where
+    C: DatabaseExecutor + Send + Sync,
+{
+    let mut amounts = get_keyset_amounts(conn, keyset_id)
+        .await?
+        .unwrap_or(KeysetAmounts {
+            total_issued: 0,
+            total_redeemed: 0,
+            fee_collected: 0,
+        });

issue.title: Migrate INTEGER/BIGINT columns storing u64 values to TEXT
issue.body:
### Description

Cashu amounts are u64, but neither SQLite nor PostgreSQL has an unsigned 64-bit integer type. Both INTEGER and BIGINT are signed, so values above `i64::MAX` silently overflow when cast to i64. This PR stores all amount-like columns as TEXT instead, eliminating the risk of truncation entirely.

Once columns become TEXT, PostgreSQL refuses to do arithmetic on them; expressions like total_issued + EXCLUDED.total_issued simply fail. Even with SQLite, casting large text values back to integers for math is unreliable. Rather than patching the SQL with ever more complex `CAST/COALESCE` chains, this PR moves all arithmetic into Rust. Each keyset amounts update now reads the current value, adds the delta with checked_add (which returns an explicit error on overflow instead of wrapping silently), and writes the result back. The same applies to SUM() aggregations — amounts are fetched as individual rows and summed in Rust.

A secondary fix handles PostgreSQL's `::` cast syntax (`column::TYPE`), which the SQL parser was misinterpreting as a named bind parameter.

As a next step, amounts should be streamed from storage rather than loaded as full result sets into memory, and all math should be performed in the mint or wallet, outside the storage layer.

issue.title: Enforce final expiry of keysetv2 keyset
issue.body:
Currently the expiry of keysetv2 is not enforced by the mint and and ecash for a keyset that has expired is still spendable. However, we should take a more strict approach here and ecash should become unspendable after the expiry. This gives the expiry a stronger meaning. 

Having a strictly enforced expiry also allows a mint operator the stop running a mint in an honest way by setting all keysets to inactive and running the mint until all keysets are expired. It also allows more unique use cases like ecash with a short expiry to encourage spending for marketing or maybe at some in person event when the ecash is only good for the weekend. 

CDK currently also enforces that there is 1 active keyset. However, for the spinning down a mint use case outlined above we should remove this.
